two_disjoint_vis_fe_ii_pools.note: RESOLVED by RYA-1229. These two published 'solar VIS Fe II DEEPGRADED' pools inside 4200-6910 A once shared NOT ONE line, and the per-line product was the side that was wrong: its generator globbed two superseded snapshot directories (rya847/gated + rya877), reading 13 of 178 per-line files. It is now a projection of the FEED, and every line of the live band product is present. ⚠️ RYA-1055's headline '0 of 11 labelled' still counts RYA-877's retired pool -- the DECK-level finding does not depend on the pool, but the count does.

mpia_grid_fill.note: The MPIA grid's Fe II half is far sparser than its Fe I half (7.1% NaN vs 0.06%). Not a defect in anything this ticket changes, and not a reason to doubt the corrections that ARE served -- but it is context for how much the Fe II NLTE label carries, and it is the mechanism behind the n-drop between an ENGINE-A leg and its LTE sibling. FOR RYA TO DISPOSITION.

rya1113_contradiction: RESOLVED. RYA-1113 found a live Fe II near-UV NLTE leg at n=7 against its LTE sibling's n=12 and asked how it can exist if Fe II NLTE is structurally unavailable, offering two answers: it is not real NLTE, or the atom has changed. BOTH ARE WRONG. The per-line artifact RYA-908 has since emitted names the source outright -- 7 lines at nlte_delta_dex = -0.001 from 'Bergemann MPIA per-line delta_nlte (live query, solar node)', 5 excluded 'ENGINE-A-NOT-SERVED'. The leg is real NLTE from the MPIA grid, a source this ticket's finding never touched, and the atom was re-measured today at still-zero Fe II bound-bound transitions. ⚠️ RYA-1113's OTHER half stands unchanged: the n=7-vs-12 gap is MPIA service coverage, so the published Fe II near-UV NLTE delta IS confounded with a 5-line pool change.

balance_note: Fe II minus Fe I on the SAME band, instrument, holding, tier, selector, route and treatment — one scale by construction, so no correction is applied to either side and no value is re-derived (RYA-161). 37 of 47 matched pairs sit inside the Fe II reported bar; the VIS 1D-NLTE (Bergemann) pairs agree to +0.0150, +0.1520, -0.1250, +0.0310, -0.1390, -0.1210, -0.1410 dex. Closest pair: solar_kpno_molecfit_corrected VIS synth-1D-LTE-gerber at -0.0020 dex (Fe II 7.460 n=6 vs Fe I 7.462 n=22). ⚠️ The Fe II bars are wide — dominated by line-to-line scatter over n=3 — so 'consistent' here means the balance does not CONTRADICT the Fe I anchor, not that it constrains it.
anchor_caveat: ⚠️ DO NOT quote the Fe II VIS cells against the 7.466 anchor directly. That anchor is on the 3D-NLTE (gold v3, RYA-553) scale and these are 1D-NLTE products; comparing them mixes two scales, which is the RYA-669 ratchet the RYA-783 report warns about in as many words. The coincidence is inviting -- the kurucz2005 Fe II cell is 7.466 to three decimals, the anchor's own digits -- and a number that looks right on arrival is the one that never gets challenged. The defensible statement is the scale-matched balance above.
verdict: CLEAN — every live Fe II product carries the limit, none takes departures from the Gerber deck, and no Fe II per-line row is on an NLTE scale
